summary: On 5 April 2022 a script meant to delete a legacy app from customer sites was given site IDs instead of app IDs. It deleted 883 sites for 775 customers, and full restoration took until 18 April.

overview.background: Atlassian had acquired the standalone app Insight - Asset Management and needed to delete the legacy app from customer sites. A script used a deletion API that accepted both site IDs and app IDs.
systems: Customer sites (Jira, Confluence, Access, Opsgenie, Statuspage)
Support tooling and customer contact data
overview.impact: 775 customers lost access to products, some for up to 14 days. No customer lost more than five minutes of data, though 57 had some databases restored to a point more than five minutes earlier.
overview.severity: Atlassian triggered its major incident process at 08:17 UTC and assigned the highest severity at 12:38.
overview.gaps: The review gives no revenue impact.

timeline.e: The deletion script begins running. Sites are deleted one after another.
The first support ticket from an affected customer is created.
The script finishes. 883 sites for 775 customers have been deleted.
Atlassian triggers its major incident process.
Teams confirm the tickets and the script run are related.
The incident is assigned the highest severity.
A second restoration process reuses original identifiers and restores the remaining sites.

rootCause.trigger: A deletion script was run with site IDs where it expected app IDs.
rootCause.underlying: The API accepted both ID types without confirming which was being deleted. Peer review focused on the endpoint, not on validating IDs, and staging could not catch it.
contributing: A communication gap between the requesting team and the runner
No soft delete: data was permanently deleted
Restoring many sites at once had not been practised
Customer contact data lived in the deleted sites, so customers could not raise tickets
propagation: Recovery takes days because restores are per site.

evidence.label: Blameless framing
evidence.body: people don’t cause incidents. Rather, systems allow for mistakes to be made.

evidence.label: Accountability
evidence.body: The buck stops with us. Full stop.

evidence.label: A simulated validation
evidence.note: Shows an API that requires the target type and extra approval for sites. Not Atlassian code.

diagnose.step: Confirm which action ran and with what input.
diagnose.why: The script run and IDs matched the deletions.

diagnose.step: Count what was deleted against what was intended.
diagnose.why: 883 sites against an intended small set.

correct.step: Stop the script and block bulk deletions.
Restore sites in batches, with new identifiers if needed.
Restore with the original identifiers for the rest.

verify.step: Check each site's data against its backup point.

verify.why: Customer contact data was lost with the sites.

prevent.step: Require staged rollout and rollback plans for deletes.
Back up contact data outside product instances.

fix.safety: Never run a destructive script on production without a dry run that prints what will be deleted, and confirm the count with a second person.

troubleshoot.scenario: A cleanup script deleted far more than intended. Customers cannot raise tickets because contact data was in the deleted sites.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do first?
hints: How do you restore at scale?
troubleshoot.answer: Stop the script, block bulk deletes, open the major incident, restore in batches, use outside channels for customers and plan better safeguards.

rootcause.q: What was wrong with the input?
options: Site IDs were given where app IDs were expected

remediation.answer: List counts and names of the objects to delete and require a second person to approve.
Mark deleted, keep for N days, purge by schedule.
Quarterly restore of a batch of sites with timing.

design.prompt: Design a deletion workflow for customer sites that cannot cause bulk loss.
design.answer: Validate IDs by type, require dry runs, soft delete with retention, staged rollout, and rate-limit deletion.

options: It was deleted with the sites

monitoring: Count of objects deleted per run
